new_candidates.duration: As proposed (not yet adopted): a six-month moratorium on data center construction, with up to two additional one-year extensions available, after which the Council of Commissioners would be required to enact permanent regulations. At its 2026-09-02 meeting, the Butte-Silver Bow Council of Commissioners voted 11-0 to direct the county attorney to prepare a temporary moratorium/interim zoning ordinance draft; no draft ordinance had been brought back for a final adoption vote as of 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Council of Commissioners motion (introduced by Commissioner Michele Shea) directing the county attorney to prepare a temporary data-center moratorium ordinance; adopted 11-0 on 2026-09-02. No ordinance number exists because the moratorium itself has not yet been adopted.
new_candidates.trigger: Ongoing local debate over data center development, including a separately litigated local ballot initiative (406 People First / Local Initiative 00-02) to require voter approval of data centers, a pending Montana Supreme Court appeal over that initiative's ballot eligibility, and public testimony citing power-supply concerns tied to a still-pending Montana Public Service Commission large-load tariff proceeding.
new_candidates.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. The Butte-Silver Bow Council of Commissioners voted 11-0 on 2026-09-02 to have the county attorney prepare a temporary data center moratorium, intended to give officials and the public more time to evaluate infrastructure, economic, environmental, and quality-of-life impacts before any new data center development proceeds. No draft ordinance had returned to the Council for final adoption as of this pass. Separately, a district court ruled against a citizens' group (406 People First) that sued the county clerk over rejected signatures for a data-center ballot initiative; that ruling is being appealed to the Montana Supreme Court, which has temporarily allowed the initiative to remain alive pending appeal (a related report indicated the initiative was ultimately kept off the November 2026 ballot).
new_candidates.affected_projects: News coverage references a company exploring potential data center sites in Silver Bow County (behind the ballot-initiative and moratorium debate), but no specific named project or MW figure was located in captured sources.
new_candidates.outcome: Council of Commissioners voted 11-0 to direct the county attorney to draft a temporary data center moratorium ordinance; not yet adopted as of this pass.

evidence.title: Butte-Silver Bow County Commission votes to pursue temporary moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the September 2, 2026 11-0 vote directing the county attorney to prepare a temporary data center moratorium, commissioner and public testimony, and the separate, related ballot-initiative litigation.
evidence.quote: Butte councilwoman Michele Shea introduced a motion for a temporary moratorium on data centers in Butte-Silver Bow County. Saying it would give the council and the public more time to consider all the information on data centers. The motion passed 11-0. ... The Butte-Silver Bow County Commission voted in favor of allowing the county attorney to prepare a temporary moratorium on data center development, as debate over the industry's future in the community continues on multiple fronts.

evidence.title: Butte commissioners discuss possibility of data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Earlier report establishing the moratorium proposal was under active consideration by the Council of Commissioners in the weeks before the September 2 vote, and specifying the proposed term (six months, with up to two one-year extensions) and that a draft zoning ordinance was due from the County Attorney.
evidence.quote: If approved, the moratorium would last for six months, with a maximum of two 1-year extensions, after which the Council of Commissioners would be required to enact regulations. ... As of last Wednesday, the Butte-Silver Bow Council of Commissioners are considering a proposal that would impose a moratorium, preventing the construction of any new data centers until further discussion is had.

new_candidates.notes: No jurisdiction disambiguation needed; Butte-Silver Bow (a consolidated city-county government) is not currently in the Montana inventory. A follow-up search for adoption of a final ordinance ('Butte-Silver Bow data center moratorium ordinance adopted') as of 2026-09-23 found only continued coverage of the September 2 direction-to-draft vote and the related ballot-initiative litigation (nbcmontana.com reported the initiative was kept off the November 2026 ballot by a judge's ruling, separate from the moratorium-drafting process), with no report of a final moratorium ordinance vote; the coordinator should re-check closer to any anticipated fall/winter Council of Commissioners meeting.
